verdict.line: You lose if you let Nasus farm Siphoning Strike stacks uncontested past level 6; you win by level 11 if you've denied CS and kept him under 50 stacks.

brief.thesis: Nasus's whole game plan is stacking Q (Siphoning Strike, cooldown 8/7/6/5/4s) on minions to scale into a late-game monster, and Illaoi's early all-in power with W (Harsh Lesson) and Tentacle procs directly punishes the minute he stops to last-hit. The data confirms it: 52.1% win rate over 1,444 games with a clear lane and solo-kill advantage for you, so this is a matchup where tempo wins, not scaling.

theirWindow.when: after he hits level 6 with 25+ stacks
theirWindow.what: Once Fury of the Sands (R) is up and his Q stacks are snowballing, Nasus's trades get scarier — his empowered Q starts doing real damage and his ultimate buys him time to free-farm. Stop contesting pure damage trades here and look for Test of Spirit (E) picks instead.

yourWindow.what: Every cast of Siphoning Strike on a minion is a window where he's rooted to a spot and not watching his flank. Walk up and Harsh Lesson (W) him off the stack attempt — it leaps you to him dealing physical damage and lets nearby Tentacles swing at him too, punishing the stack far harder than the CS was worth.

start.why: The lifesteal and AD sustain you through repeated W-ins on his farm attempts without needing to back off lane; it's the standard start in 71.9% of games for a reason.

boots.why: Nasus's only real poke pre-6 is auto-attack trades during stack fights, and the flat physical damage reduction blunts every one of those exchanges.

core.why: Armor shred stacks fast in extended W/Q trades and keeps your damage relevant as his health pool grows from Soul Eater lifesteal.
The attack-speed and slow proc helps you stick to him after a W leap so he can't just walk away and reset to farming.
Survives his all-in once Fury of the Sands is online, since that ultimate's max-health drain is the one real threat he has against you.

situational.when: he's building AP/on-hit heal items and outscaling your raw damage
his Soul Eater lifesteal is keeping him alive through your trades
you need to survive extended all-ins post-6 without giving up damage

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp rewards exactly the playstyle this matchup wants — walking up and trading autos/W on him every time he goes for a stack — while building the health that lets you win extended skirmishes.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 19.5% of games at a 55.5% win rate, the highest of the three common pages — Ignite seals the solo-kill advantage this matchup already gives you before he can sustain it off with lifesteal.

playing.title: Punish every stack attempt
playing.detail: Whenever Nasus commits to Siphoning Strike on a minion, he's stationary for a beat — walk up and Harsh Lesson (W) him immediately; the leap plus nearby Tentacle swings outvalue the CS he was going for.

playing.title: Use Test of Spirit to zone, not just damage
playing.detail: E (Test of Spirit, cooldown 16-12s) rips his spirit out and echoes damage back to him — use it before trades to add extra chip damage, and remember it also sets up a Vessel if he dies or disengages too far.

playing.title: Don't greed past level 8 even
playing.detail: Once he's six-plus and his Q stacks are climbing, his trades hit harder and his ultimate buys him free farming time — shift to poking with Q (Tentacle Smash) and E rather than standing in extended melee exchanges.

playing.title: Track his Q stack count, not just his level
playing.detail: A level 9 Nasus with 40 stacks is a different fight than one with 15 — if you've been denying CS all lane, he's weaker than his level implies and you should keep pressing.

playing.title: Ignite-secure your early kills
playing.detail: Illaoi has the solo-kill edge in this matchup already; Ignite turns a close all-in around level 3-5 into a guaranteed kill before he can Wither (W) and run.

playing.title: Respect Fury of the Sands cooldown, not just its existence
playing.detail: His ultimate is on a 120-second cooldown — if you track when he's used it, you get a clean window afterward to all-in without the max-health drain threat.

playing.title: Don't let armor shred go to waste
playing.detail: Black Cleaver stacks reward sustained contact — commit to full trades once you've got 2-3 stacks on him rather than disengaging early.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the matchup read — why the stack-punish pattern works and when the power shifts — is my own tactical analysis layered on top of the ability text.

stats.opponentTip: Harass Nasus while laning to prevent him from gaining stacks through (Q). Illaoi has the upper hand during early and mid-game, so use this to your advantage to engage when possible.
